quotes.text: the probable cause of this accident was the failure of the Aloha Airlines maintenance program to detect the presence of significant disbonding and fatigue damage which ultimately led to failure of the lap joint at S-10L and the separation of the fuselage upper lobe. Contributing to the accident were the failure of Aloha Airlines management to supervise properly its maintenance force; the failure of the FAA to require Airworthiness Directive 87-21-08 inspection of all the lap joints proposed by Boeing Alert Service Bulletin SB 737-53A1039; and the lack of a complete terminating action (neither generated by Boeing nor required by the FAA) after the discovery of early production difficulties in the B-737 cold-bond lap joint, which resulted in low bond durability, corrosion, and premature fatigue cracking.
quotes.speaker: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) final report

timeline.event: Aloha Airlines begins operating passenger flights.
Aloha Airlines places an order for two Boeing 737-200 jetliners.
The Boeing 737-297 involved in the accident, line number 152 registered as N73711, is manufactured.
The Boeing 737-200 jets named "Funbirds" enter service with Aloha Airlines.
The first of three unsuccessful merger attempts between Aloha Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines is made.
Ching and vice-chairman Sheridan Ing announce plans to take Aloha Airlines private after surviving hostile takeover bids.
The aircraft completes three uneventful round-trip flights between Honolulu and Hilo, Maui, and Kauai.
Passenger Gayle Yamamoto notices a crack in the fuselage upon boarding the aircraft but does not notify anyone.
Aloha Airlines Flight 243 departs bound for Honolulu with 5 crew members and 90 passengers on board.
A section on the left side of the roof ruptures and a large section of the roof tears off, ejecting flight attendant Clarabelle "C.B." Lansing.
timeline.place: About 23 nautical miles (43 km; 26 mi) south-southeast of Kahului on Maui

timeline.event: Emergency evacuation slides are deployed, passengers evacuate, Akamai drivers establish a triage on the runway, and tour vans transport the injured to the hospital.
The heavily damaged aircraft is dismantled on site and written off.
Aloha Airlines makes a second unsuccessful merger attempt with Hawaiian Airlines.
The story of Flight 243 is made into the television movie Miracle Landing.
A memorial garden is opened in Terminal 1 of Honolulu International Airport in honor of Clarabelle Lansing.
The Canadian television series Mayday features the accident in the season-three episode "Hanging by a Thread".
Flight 243 is featured in the Mayday season six Science of Disaster special titled "Ripped Apart".
